_meta.description: Karnataka district & sessions court formatting rules — drives cause-title, party designations, prayer language, verification format
_meta.change_protocol: CLO sign-off required for any change. Vishal raises Jira tickets to Ajay for additions; never edits unilaterally.

designation: IN THE COURT OF DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE
jurisdictionNote: District-level criminal and civil courts in Karnataka. Sessions courts try offences punishable with imprisonment exceeding 7 years. Magistrate-level criminal cases are commonly numbered as C.C. (Calendar Case) in Karnataka. Bengaluru Urban operates as the City Civil & Sessions Court under the Karnataka Civil Courts Act, 1964 and allied Karnataka High Court rules.

party_designation.state: State of Karnataka through the Principal Secretary, Home Department, Government of Karnataka, Bengaluru

prayer_language.opening: It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to:
prayer_language.closing: And for this act of kindness, the petitioner shall, as in duty bound, ever pray.

verification_format:
I, {deponent_name}, {designation}, do hereby solemnly affirm and declare that the contents of the above petition from paragraph ___ to paragraph ___ are true to my personal knowledge and the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ are believed to be true on the basis of information received and legal advice tendered, which I believe to be true. Nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Solemnly affirmed at {place} on this {date}.

DEPONENT
localRules: Bail applications under S.483 BNSS must disclose any earlier rejection by the Magistrate or any co-ordinate court.
Anticipatory bail applications (S.482 BNSS) must be accompanied by an affidavit and a certified copy of the FIR.
Vakalatnama in the form prescribed under the Karnataka Civil Rules of Practice / Karnataka High Court Rules to be filed at the first instance with the requisite court-fee stamp.
All civil pleadings to be paginated, indexed and accompanied by a list of documents under Order VII / Order VIII CPC.
Kannada translation may be insisted upon for documents in English where parties are not conversant; cf. Karnataka Official Language Act, 1963 and Karnataka Civil Rules of Practice.
In Bengaluru, plaints before the City Civil & Sessions Court are valued under the Karnataka Civil Courts Act, 1964; pecuniary limits periodically revised by State Govt. notification.
Service of summons in Bengaluru is supplemented by registered post AD under Karnataka Civil Rules of Practice.
Atrocities (SC/ST) cases, POCSO cases and NDPS cases are tried by designated Special Courts notified by the State Government.
e_filing_note: e-Filing is operational at Bengaluru City Civil & Sessions Court and select district HQs via the eCourts portal; not yet mandatory state-wide.
